1-2.word_for_word: अष्टाशीतितमे विष्णु-भक्तः कैवल्यम् अश्नुते । — In the eighty-eighth year, a devotee of Lord Vishnu attains Kaivalya.; ततोऽर्वाग्-देव-भक्तस् तु विभूतिम् इति वर्ण्यते ॥ — After that, the devotee of the Lord of the Arvāg-devas is described as Vibhūti.; हरिर् भजतां मुक्तिद इत्य् उक्तम् अभयं ध्यायेद् अजस्रं हरिम् [भा।पु। — It is said that Hari is the giver of liberation to those who worship Him.; १०.८७.५४] इति तत्र शङ्कते---देवासुरेति । — 10.87.54] There he suspects that they are gods and demons.; अशिवम् अवधीरित-भोगम् । — Ashivam avadhirita-bhogam.; भोजा भोगिनः । — Bhoja is the enjoyer.; लक्ष्म्याः पतिं सर्व-भोग-युक्तम् ॥ — The husband of Lakshmi is endowed with all pleasures.; १-२ ॥ — 1-2 ॥
1-2.translation: In the eighty-eighth year, a devotee of Lord Vishnu attains Kaivalya. After that, the devotee of the Lord of the Arvāg-devas is described as Vibhūti. It is said that Hari is the giver of liberation to those who worship Him. 10.87.54] There he suspects that they are gods and demons. Ashivam avadhirita-bhogam. Bhoja is the enjoyer. The husband of Lakshmi is endowed with all pleasures. 1-2 ॥

3.word_for_word: अन्योन्योपमर्देन तमसस् त्रैविध्यस् त्रिलिङ्गः । — The threefold nature of darkness is the threefold nature of the universe by rubbing against each other.; त्रिलिङ्गत्वम् आह---वैकारिक इति । — He argues that the trilingualism is transformational.; अहम् अहङ्कार इति ॥३॥ — I am the ego.
3.translation: The threefold nature of darkness is the threefold nature of the universe by rubbing against each other. He argues that the trilingualism is transformational. I am the ego.

4.word_for_word: विकारा मन-इन्द्रिय-भूत-रूपाः । — The transformations are the forms of the mind, senses and ghosts.; षोडशेतीन्द्रिय-देवानाम् अभेद-विवक्षया । — By describing the differences between the sixteen sense-gods.; कंचन यत् किञ्चिद् विकारोपाधिकं भजन्न् उपाध्य्-अनुरूपाणां विभूतीनां स्वरूपं प्राप्नोतीति ॥४॥ — By worshiping anything that is the means of transformation one attains the form of the opulences corresponding to the means.
4.translation: The transformations are the forms of the mind, senses and ghosts. By describing the differences between the sixteen sense-gods. By worshiping anything that is the means of transformation one attains the form of the opulences corresponding to the means.

5.word_for_word:
उपद्रष्टा साक्षी सन् । — being an observer and a witness.; यतः सर्व-दृक् सर्वं पश्यति । — Because the all-seeing sees everything.; अतः प्रकृतेः पर इति । — Therefore, it is beyond nature.; अत्रेदं तत्त्वं--- — Here is the fact; > वस्तुनो गुण-सम्बन्धे रूप-द्वयम् इहेष्यते । — > Two forms are here mentioned in relation to the properties of the object.; >
> तद्-धर्मायोग-योगाभ्यां बिम्बवत् प्रतिबिम्बवत् ॥ — >
> That is like an image, like a reflection, by the combination of dharma and yoga.; >
> गुणाः सत्त्वादयः शान्त-घोर-मूढाः स्वभावतः । — >
> The modes of nature, such as Sattva, are calm, terrible and foolish by nature.; >
> विष्णु-ब्रह्म-शिवानां च गुण-यन्तृ-स्वरूपिणाम् ॥ — >
> They are the modes of nature of Lord Viṣṇu, Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva.; >
> नातिभेदो भवेद् भेदो गुण-धर्मैर् इहांशतः । — >
> There should be no difference in the qualities and characteristics of the parties here.; >
> सत्त्वस्य शान्त्या नो जातु विष्णोर् विक्षेपम् ऊढते ॥ — >
> By the peace of the mode of goodness, we never become distracted by Lord Viṣṇu.; >
> रजस्-तमो-गुणाभ्यां तु भवेतां ब्रह्म-रुद्रयोः । — >
> The modes of passion and darkness are the two modes of nature, Brahma and Rudra.; >
> गुणोपमर्दतो भूयस् तद्-अंशानां च भिन्नता ॥ — >
> The difference between the modes of nature and their parts is greater.; >
> अतः समग्र-सत्त्वस्य विष्णोर् मोक्ष-करी मतिः । — >
> Therefore, the mind of Vishnu is the liberator of the entire being.; >
> अंशतो भूति-हेतुश् च तथानन्द-मयी स्वतः ॥ — >
> In part she is the cause of happiness and in her own right she is full of bliss.; >
> अंशतस् तारतम्येन ब्रह्म-रुद्रादि-सेविनाम् । — >
> In part, by the continuity of the worshipers of Brahma, Rudra and others.; >
> विभूतयो भवन्त्य् एव शनैर् मोक्षोऽप्य् अनंशतः ॥ — >
> The glories are slowly attained, and even liberation is partially attained.; इदम् एवाभिप्रेत्य तत्र तत्रोच्यते श्रेयांसि तत्र खलु सत्त्व-तनोर् नृणां स्युः [भा।पु। — With this in mind, it is said here and there that the best things are there indeed for men of the body of Sattva [Bh.p.; १.२.२३] इति । — 1.2.23] is the source.; तथा सत्त्वं यस्य प्रिया मूर्तिः [भा।पु। — and the Sattva whose beloved idol [Bh.p.; १०.८९.१८] इति । — 10.89.18] is the source.; तथा सत्त्वं तत् तीर्थ-साधनम् [भा।पु। — and Sattva is that means of pilgrimage [Bh.p.; १०.८९.१९] इति तथा, त्रयाणाम् एक-भावानां यो न पश्यति वै भिदाम् [भा।पु। — 10.89.19] Thus, he who does not see the difference between the three one-beings [Bh.p.; ४.७.५४] इति । — 4.7.54] is the same.; तथा, न ते मय्य् अच्युतेऽजे च भिदाम् अण्व् अपि चक्षते [भा।पु। — Thus, they do not even taste the difference between Me, the Acyuta and the Aja [Bh.p.; १२.१०.२२] इत्य् आदि । — 12.10.22] and so on.; एवं च सति न किञ्चिद् असमञ्जसम् । — In this case, there is nothing inconsistent.; तत्-तद्-भक्तानां तु कलहो मोह-मात्रम् इति ॥ — For those who are devoted to that, quarreling is only delusion.; ५-७ ॥ — 5-7 ॥
5.translation:
being an observer and a witness. Because the all-seeing sees everything. Therefore, it is beyond nature. Here is the fact > Two forms are here mentioned in relation to the properties of the object. >
> That is like an image, like a reflection, by the combination of dharma and yoga. >
> The modes of nature, such as Sattva, are calm, terrible and foolish by nature. >
> They are the modes of nature of Lord Viṣṇu, Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva. >
> There should be no difference in the qualities and characteristics of the parties here. >
> By the peace of the mode of goodness, we never become distracted by Lord Viṣṇu. >
> The modes of passion and darkness are the two modes of nature, Brahma and Rudra. >
> The difference between the modes of nature and their parts is greater. >
> Therefore, the mind of Vishnu is the liberator of the entire being. >
> In part she is the cause of happiness and in her own right she is full of bliss. >
> In part, by the continuity of the worshipers of Brahma, Rudra and others. >
> The glories are slowly attained, and even liberation is partially attained. With this in mind, it is said here and there that the best things are there indeed for men of the body of Sattva [Bh.p. 1.2.23] is the source. and the Sattva whose beloved idol [Bh.p. 10.89.18] is the source. and Sattva is that means of pilgrimage [Bh.p. 10.89.19] Thus, he who does not see the difference between the three one-beings [Bh.p. 4.7.54] is the same. Thus, they do not even taste the difference between Me, the Acyuta and the Aja [Bh.p. 12.10.22] and so on. In this case, there is nothing inconsistent. For those who are devoted to that, quarreling is only delusion. 5-7 ॥

8.word_for_word: यस्याहम् अनुगृह्णामीति । — to whom I am gracious.; अयम् अर्थः । — This is the meaning.; यो विषयान् परिजिहीर्षुर् अपि कथञ्चिद् विद्यमानेषु विषयेषु सज्जते, क्लिश्यते च, तस्य विषयापहार एवानुग्रह इति । — For one who, even though he wishes to conquer objects, is somehow attached to and tormented by the objects that exist, the deprivation of objects is grace.; यथाश्रुतत्वे धुर्वादीनाम् ऐश्वर्य-विरोधात्, अथवा प्रथमं विभूतीः कामानुरूपा दत्त्वा शनैर् विषय-भोगावसाने तस्य निर्वेदम् उत्पाद्य हरिष्यामि, परमानुग्रहं कर्तुम् इति । — As I have heard, because of the contradiction of the wealth of the Dhurvadis, or because I first give them the glories according to their desires, and slowly, at the end of their sense gratification, I produce their indifference and take them away, in order to show them supreme mercy.; तद् उक्तं भगवतैव---न मय्य् आवेशित-धियां कामः कामाय कल्पते [भा।पु। — That is what the Lord Himself said: Desire is not fit for desire in the mind fixed on Me [Bh.p.; १०.२२.२६] इति । — 10.22.26] is the same.; दुःख-दुःखितम् इति । — It is suffering-suffering.; दुःखाद् अनु पुनर्-दुःखितम् इव प्रतीयमानम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥८॥ — This means that it seems to be suffering again and again after suffering.
8.translation: to whom I am gracious. This is the meaning. For one who, even though he wishes to conquer objects, is somehow attached to and tormented by the objects that exist, the deprivation of objects is grace. As I have heard, because of the contradiction of the wealth of the Dhurvadis, or because I first give them the glories according to their desires, and slowly, at the end of their sense gratification, I produce their indifference and take them away, in order to show them supreme mercy. That is what the Lord Himself said: Desire is not fit for desire in the mind fixed on Me [Bh.p. 10.22.26] is the same. It is suffering-suffering. This means that it seems to be suffering again and again after suffering.

9.word_for_word: स पुनर् बन्धूनाम् आग्रहेण धनेहया प्रवृत्तोऽपि मद्-अनुग्रहेण यदा निष्फलोद्यमो निर्विण्णः स्यात् तदा मद्-अनुग्रहम् इति ममासाधारणम् अनुग्रहम् ॥९॥ — He again, at the insistence of his relatives, engaged in the pursuit of wealth, but by My grace, when his fruitless endeavor becomes frustrated, it is My extraordinary grace.
9.translation: He again, at the insistence of his relatives, engaged in the pursuit of wealth, but by My grace, when his fruitless endeavor becomes frustrated, it is My extraordinary grace.

10.word_for_word: तम् एवाह---तद् ब्रह्मेति । — He said to himself, "That is Brahman.; अतः पश्चाद् अपि मोक्षम् अरोचयन् । — Therefore they did not desire liberation even afterwards.; अत्य्-आसक्तो जन इत्य् अर्थः ॥ — This means that people are very attached.; १०-११ ॥ — 10-11 ॥
10.translation: He said to himself, "That is Brahman. Therefore they did not desire liberation even afterwards. This means that people are very attached. 10-11 ॥

12.word_for_word: एतद् एवेतिहासेन स्पष्टयितुम् आह शाप-प्रसादयोर् इति ब्रह्मा चेत्य् अन्वयः ॥ — To explain this very fact by history, he argues that the curse and the grace are the same, and that the Brahman is the consequence.; १२-१३ ॥ — 12-13.
12.translation: To explain this very fact by history, he argues that the curse and the grace are the same, and that the Brahman is the consequence. 12-13.

14.word_for_word: शकुनेः पुत्रः ॥ — The son of Shakuni.; १४-१५ ॥ — 14-15.

16.word_for_word: सुसङ्कटम् आप कैलासोत्पाटनं पुरपालनं च ॥१६॥ — The uprooting of Kailas and the maintenance of the city were in great danger
16.translation: The uprooting of Kailas and the maintenance of the city were in great danger

17.word_for_word: स्वगात्रत उपाधावत् कथम् आत्मक्रव्येण स्व-मांसेन जुह्वान इति ॥१७॥ — How could he run from his own body and offer sacrifices with his own flesh?
17.translation: How could he run from his own body and offer sacrifices with his own flesh?

19.word_for_word: मूर्तिमान् अग्निर् इव देदीप्यमानः वयम् अधुनातना यथाकिञ्चिद्-दुःखेन मर्तुकामं वारयामस् तद्वद् इति स च उपस्-कृताकृतिः परिपूर्ण-देहो\ऽभवत् तं न्यवारयद् एवमाह च ॥१९॥ — In the form of a fire burning like fire we now with some pain restrain the desire to die in the same way as we restrain the desire to die Thus he assumed the form of a worshiper and became full of body restrained him and said thus.
19.translation: In the form of a fire burning like fire we now with some pain restrain the desire to die in the same way as we restrain the desire to die Thus he assumed the form of a worshiper and became full of body restrained him and said thus.

20.word_for_word: तोयेनापि भजतां प्रीतः स्यां त्वया तु देहो वृथापीड्यत इति ॥ — I shall be pleased with those who worship me even with water, but you are tormenting my body in vain.; २०-२१ ॥ — 20-21.
20.translation: I shall be pleased with those who worship me even with water, but you are tormenting my body in vain. 20-21.

22.word_for_word: दातुम् अनर्हम् अपि दत्तवान् सर्पय क्षीरम् इव ॥ — He gave it to someone who didn’t deserve it, just as a snake gives milk to a snake.; २२-२३ ॥ — 22-23.
22.translation: He gave it to someone who didn’t deserve it, just as a snake gives milk to a snake. 22-23.

24.word_for_word: उपसृष्टोऽनुगतः सन् उद्गादावत् उद्गुत्ततः ॥२४॥ — He was approached and followed as if he had been raised from the ground.
24.translation: He was approached and followed as if he had been raised from the ground.

25-27.word_for_word: द्विजेरितं साधु साध्विति घोषं श्रुत्वा हार्दम् अभिप्रायम् ॥ — Hearing the cry of the brāhmaṇas, “Well done, well done,” I felt heartfelt intention.; २६-३१ ॥ — 26-31.; वैकुण्ठं श्वेत-द्वीपम् ॥ — Vaikuntha is the white island.; २५-२६ ॥ — 25-26.; तं वृकासुरम् । — That’s the wolf demon.; तथा-व्यसनं तादृग् व्यसनं यस्य तम् । — and-addiction to such addiction.; वृजिनार्दनो दुःख-हन्ता । — He is the destroyer of sorrows and the destroyer of suffering.; दूरत एव दृष्ट्वा मेखलादिभिर् उपलक्षितः प्रत्युदियात् संमुखम् आगतः ॥ — Seeing him from a distance, he was recognized by his belt and other weapons, and he rose up and came in front of him.; २७-२८ ॥ — 27-28.
25-27.translation: Hearing the cry of the brāhmaṇas, “Well done, well done,” I felt heartfelt intention. 26-31. Vaikuntha is the white island. 25-26. That’s the wolf demon. and-addiction to such addiction. He is the destroyer of sorrows and the destroyer of suffering. Seeing him from a distance, he was recognized by his belt and other weapons, and he rose up and came in front of him. 27-28.

29.word_for_word: व्यक्तं निश्चितम् । — Obviously, it’s certain.; किं किम् अर्थम् । — What does it mean?; आत्मा देहः सर्व-पुरुषार्थ-हेतुः । — The soul is the body, the cause of all human purposes.; अतो मा पीडयेति ॥२९॥ — Therefore do not torment me.
29.translation: Obviously, it’s certain. What does it mean? The soul is the body, the cause of all human purposes. Therefore do not torment me.

30.word_for_word: प्रायशः पुम्भिर् दृतैर् भवान् स्वार्थान् समीहते साधयितुम् इच्छति । — You usually try to achieve your own goals by being given by men.; अथवा जनः पुम्भिः सहायैः स्व-कार्याणि साधयत्य् अतो नः कथ्यताम् इति ॥३०॥ — Or else people accomplish their affairs with the help of men, therefore tell us.
30.translation: You usually try to achieve your own goals by being given by men. Or else people accomplish their affairs with the help of men, therefore tell us.

32.word_for_word: पैशाच्यं पिशाचानाम् इव वृत्तिम् ॥ — It is like the behavior of devils.; ३२-३३ ॥ — 32-33.
32.translation: It is like the behavior of devils. 32-33.

34.word_for_word: यद् यथा । — That’s like.; वक्ता वदिष्यति ॥३४॥ — The speaker will speak.
34.translation: That’s like. The speaker will speak.

35.word_for_word: चित्रैर् भ्रामकैः सु-पेशलैर् अति-रम्यैः । — They are picturesque and very beautiful.; भिन्न-धीर् भ्रंशित-मतिः ॥३५॥ — He is of a different mind and a destroyed mind.
35.translation: They are picturesque and very beautiful. He is of a different mind and a destroyed mind.

38.word_for_word: किमु वक्तव्यं विश्वेशे त्वयि कृतागस्कः कृतापराध इति ॥३८॥ — What can I say, O Lord of the universe, that I have committed an offense against You?
38.translation: What can I say, O Lord of the universe, that I have committed an offense against You?

40.word_for_word: अव्याकृत-शक्त्य्-उदन्वतो वाङ् मनसागोचर-शक्ति-समुद्रस्य । — From the ocean of unmanifest energy, which flows from speech and from the mind, is the ocean of energy.; गिरित्र-मोक्षं शिव-मोचन-रूपं चरितम् । — The character of Giritra Moksha is the form of Lord Shiva’s liberation.; संसृतिभिर् नाना-योनि-सञ्चारैः ॥४०॥ — by the movements of various sexual intercourses.
40.translation: From the ocean of unmanifest energy, which flows from speech and from the mind, is the ocean of energy. The character of Giritra Moksha is the form of Lord Shiva’s liberation. by the movements of various sexual intercourses.
